previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory conditions was admitted for green, blood-tinged sputum, dyspnea, and throat pain. She had no fever, stable vital signs, and normal white blood cell count. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and ENT tracheoscopy revealed no signs of tracheal inflammation or infection. Given the absence of bacterial infection markers, antibiotics were withheld, and she was managed symptomatically for an acute upper respiratory infection. Her chronic pain was controlled with home medications, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor for red flag symptoms and to follow up with ENT. Chronic issues, including iron deficiency anemia and diarrhea, were noted for outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year-old female with a PMH of tracheobronchomalacia secondary 
to premature birth at ___, s/p 4 airway reconstructions and 
tracheostomy since infancy, h/o chronic bronchitits and 
tracheitis, h/o chronic pain on narcotics contract presents with 
dyspnea and green sputum production 4 days concerning for 
recurrent tracheitis. 

#Viral URI: Pt presented with four days of increased green 
sputum production with cough, subjective chills, worsening 
throat pain. Physical exam, lab work, CXR unremarkable. Patient 
was observed over night and did well, afebrile, no leukocytosis, 
and did not demonstrate a high suction requirement for 
secretions. Her pain was well controlled with her oral home 
regimen. Tracheoscopy by ENT revealed no evidence of infection,  
normal tracheal mucosa, pink, moist, without any erythema or 
purulence. No secretions visualized from trach entry site to 
carina. Patient refused nasopharyngoscopy. Antibiotics held as 
c/f bacterial tracheobronchitis is very low.

vs delta-beta thalassemia). No signs of active bleeding

initial Hgb was accurate. Discharge H/H 8.7/29.7.

All other home medications were continued and the patient was  
discharged without any changes to her home medications. She has  
ENT follow up scheduled.
